w10_T4_002193: Cal began the quiz night with 228 points on his scorecard, which was already more than his rival Dot had. He lost 11 points on a wrong answer, and then a jackpot question made his score 3 times what it was. Two hard rounds cost him 211 points and then 146 points. In the final round every point still on his card was worth 4 points. How many points did Cal finish with?
w10_T4_002202: The village library's history shelf held 206 books at the start of the year. In February 14 books were donated to the shelf, in April 68 books arrived from a closing school library, and in June 55 books were bought with a grant. The library is open 6 days a week. In September 31 books were added from a retired teacher's collection, and in November 22 more were bought. How many books are on the history shelf now?
w10_T4_002204: In the morning Eve's rainwater tank held 79 litres. A shower before noon added 8 litres to the tank. In the afternoon a heavy downpour added 39 litres and then a second storm added 60 litres. In the evening a light drizzle added 14 litres more. Eve reads the tank in litres rather than millilitres, since one thousand millilitres make a litre. How many litres are in the tank now?
w10_T4_002206: Fen had 139 dollars, received 35 dollars for her birthday, and then spent 158 dollars on a jacket. Her brother Gil earns 2 times as much in a day as Fen had left after buying the jacket, so Gil's daily pay is more than Fen's remaining money. Gil worked 8 days this fortnight. He then spent 115 dollars on a train ticket and 4 dollars on a coffee. How many dollars does Gil have left from this fortnight's pay?
w10_T4_002211: Hana's coin jar receives 73 cents from each of the 8 people in her house every Monday, plus a 28-cent contribution from the neighbour's boy. Every week she takes 430 cents out of the jar for the shared milk order and puts 72 cents of bottle refunds back in. That weekly amount is more than her friend Ivo manages to save in his own jar. She kept exactly to this pattern for 4 weeks, starting from an empty jar. Hana counts in cents rather than dollars, remembering that one hundred cents make a dollar. How many cents are in the jar after those 4 weeks?
w10_T4_002214: Jon started the year with 227 stamps in his collection. He traded 27 stamps away at a fair, and then received 52 stamps from an uncle, 30 stamps from a friend, and 65 stamps from an online swap. His sister Kim collects too, but she still has fewer stamps than Jon. How many stamps does Jon have now?
w10_T4_002216: In the morning a print shop packed a box of leaflets for a campaign: 121 leaflets from the first run, 8 leaflets from a reprint, and 70 leaflets from the second run. A pack is made of twice that many leaflets, 2 boxes packed identically, plus 52 loose leaflets slipped in on top. In the afternoon 5 packs were loaded into each van. In the evening 9 vans set off with those loads. How many leaflets were sent out that evening?
w10_T4_002217: Lia's small farm produces 191 kilograms of tomatoes a week. Max's farm produces 3 times as much per week as Lia's does, so Max's harvest is far larger, and Max also picks 57 kilograms of cherry tomatoes each week. The season lasts 9 weeks, and Max sells 4938 kilograms of his season's crop to a cannery. He sells every remaining kilogram at the farm gate for 2 dollars a kilogram. How many dollars does Max make at the farm gate?
w10_T4_002218: Nell had 155 tomato seeds in a packet. She planted 153 of them in the greenhouse and dropped 1 seed down a drain, then bought a packet of 69 more seeds. Her garden is 15 metres long. Every seed she now had grew into a plant that produced 8 tomatoes, which Nell thought was a fine result after a dozen years of gardening. Her family ate 267 of the tomatoes and she sold 200 at the gate. How many tomatoes are left?
w10_T4_002226: The bake sale started with 201 cupcakes on the main table, but 14 were eaten by the helpers and 33 more were brought in by a late parent. There were 5 tables at the sale, each with exactly the same number of cupcakes as the main table. The sale ran for 3 hours. At the end, all of the cupcakes were shared equally among 4 charities. How many cupcakes did the hospice charity receive?
w10_T4_002229: At the parcel depot each cage holds 238 parcels, each trolley carries 3 cages, and each van is loaded with 3 trolleys. The depot is 20 kilometres from the airport. The depot sends out 7 fully loaded vans every day, and the manager, who has worked there for a dozen years, counted the parcels sent out over a 3-day weekend. How many parcels were sent out over the weekend?
w10_T4_002233: Ola had 184 dollars in her savings jar. For her birthday her grandfather doubled what was in the jar, and her aunt added 10 dollars. Ola then took 340 dollars out of the jar to buy a laptop. After that her mother put 69 dollars into the jar for good exam results. How many dollars are in Ola's jar now?
w10_T4_002235: Pat had 133 cents in his pocket, spent 38 cents on a stamp, and then found 13 cents in the car. His cousin Quil had 5 times as many cents as Pat had at that point, so Quil was the richer of the two. Quil then earned 42 cents returning a shopping trolley and spent 579 cents on a book. Quil counts in cents rather than dollars, knowing that one hundred cents make a dollar. How many cents does Quil have left?
w10_T4_002239: In the morning Rob picked 20 plums from the garden tree, and his sister Sue picked 2 times as many plums as Rob did, so Sue's basket was fuller. Sue split her plums equally into 2 bags and gave 1 bag to their grandmother. In the afternoon Sue picked 58 more plums. In the evening she divided all the plums she had equally into 3 jars for jam, and then used 18 plums from the first jar for a pie. How many plums are left in the first jar?
w10_T4_002244: Each of Tia's hens gets a feed made of 129 grams of grain, 44 grams of seed, and 76 grams of greens at every feeding, and Tia feeds her hens 3 times a day. She has 2 hens, which eat more between them than her neighbour Ugo's whole flock. She fed them this way for 5 days and also gave them 46 grams of dried worms as a treat. Tia weighs feed in grams rather than kilograms, since one thousand grams make a kilogram. How many grams of food did Tia's hens eat over those 5 days?
w10_T4_002250: Val's craft stall took in 101 dollars on Saturday, but she had to give a 42-dollar refund, and then a late customer spent 65 dollars. Wes's stall takes in 7 times as much in a day as Val's did that Saturday, so Wes is doing far better than Val. Wes traded for 6 days at that daily rate. How many dollars did Wes take in over those 6 days?
w10_T4_002256: In the morning a fruit seller opened 4 crates of apples with 177 apples in each and sold 595 apples before lunch, then found 10 apples in the bottom of an empty crate. In the afternoon he threw away 12 bruised apples and sold every remaining apple at 9 cents each. In the evening he paid 708 cents to the farmer for the crates. He keeps his books in cents rather than dollars, remembering that one hundred cents make a dollar. How many cents did the seller have left from the afternoon's sales after paying the farmer?
w10_T4_002262: Xan had 140 dollars in his savings account. He spent half of it on a bicycle, and then deposited 26 dollars from his paper round. A savings scheme at his bank then made his balance 4 times what it was. Xan then withdrew 349 dollars for a school trip. How many dollars are in Xan's account now?
w10_T4_002265: Yui's bakery bakes 8 trays of pastries every morning with 177 pastries on each tray. Zac's bakery, which is much bigger, bakes twice as many pastries each morning as Yui's does. This morning Zac gave 228 pastries to a homeless shelter, sold 2305 pastries to customers, and threw away 257 pastries that had burned. How many pastries does Zac have left?
w10_T4_002269: In the morning the tip jar at Ari's cafe held 25 dollars, and Ari took 16 dollars out of it to pay the milkman. A generous regular then matched what was left, making the jar hold 2 times as much. In the afternoon customers added 77 dollars and then 25 dollars to the jar. In the evening the jar was shared equally among the 4 staff on duty. The cafe counts tips in dollars rather than cents, since one hundred cents make a dollar. How many dollars did Ari receive from the jar?
w10_T4_002270: On Saturday morning Cara's bakery had 193 loaves on its shelves, which was more than Ben's bakery next door had baked, and it sold 176 loaves before noon. In the afternoon Cara sold 11 more loaves and dropped 1 loaf on the floor, which had to be thrown away. In the evening a customer returned 4 loaves that had been ordered by mistake, and Cara cut every loaf still on the shelves into 2 halves to sell at the night market. How many half-loaves did Cara take to the night market?
w10_T4_002271: Dan was paid 80 cents for each of the 9 windows he washed on Saturday, and he shared the money equally among the 5 friends who had helped him, one of whom was Eli. The job took 3 hours. Eli then found 66 cents on the pavement and spent 68 cents on an ice cream, which still left Eli with less money than Dan had kept for himself. Eli counts in cents rather than dollars, knowing that one hundred cents make a dollar. How many cents does Eli have now?
w10_T4_002272: In the morning Fia had 20 cookies in her lunchbox and gave half of them to her friend. In the afternoon her mother refilled the box so that Fia had twice as many cookies as she had after sharing, and then Fia ate half of what was in the box. In the evening her grandmother baked 29 cookies and put them all in the box. How many cookies are in Fia's lunchbox now?
w10_T4_002273: A film crew shot 148 minutes of footage for a series and divided it equally among 4 episodes. From the first episode the editor cut an 8-minute scene and an 18-minute scene, then added 72 minutes of newly shot material after a dozen days of reshoots. The editor logs footage in minutes rather than hours, since sixty minutes make one hour. How many minutes long is the first episode now?
w10_T4_002277: Gia's factory runs 8 identical machines, each producing 132 bottle caps an hour, and a worker adds 3 caps an hour by hand. The factory has 40 workers in all. The machines run 7 hours a day, 3 days a week, and the order runs for 9 weeks, which is more caps than Hal's rival factory could make in that time. Of the caps made for the order, 95661 failed inspection and were scrapped. How many caps passed inspection?
